title: The open/closed comparison commutes with closure extension identifications
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite discrete commutative ring. Use ordinary derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $C_W=\nu_W^*$ for the exact etale/pro-etale comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. For an open immersion $j$ [def-weil-open-immersion], let $o_j:C_Xj_{e,!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{p,!}C_U$ be the termwise canonical open comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], using extensions by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero], and let $a_j:C_Uj_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_p^*C_X$ be the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. For a closed immersion $h:Z\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], let $\delta_h:C_XRh_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{p,*}C_Z$ on $D^+$ be the specified counit-mate comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], and let $a_h:C_Zh_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h_p^*C_X$ be canonical pullback comparison. Subscripts $e,p$ mean etale and pro-etale. Composition is read right to left.

Let $T$ be Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], let $s:S\hookrightarrow T$ be an immersion with factorization $s=v\circ c$ (closed then open), and let $(u:S\hookrightarrow\bar S,i:\bar S\hookrightarrow T)$ be its scheme-theoretic closure factorization (open then closed) [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Here $\bar S=\operatorname{SIm}(s)$ is the closed subscheme cut out by the largest quasi-coherent ideal contained in $\ker(\mathcal O_T\to s_*\mathcal O_S)$; $i$ is its image inclusion and $u$ its canonical factor map. These immersions into the Noetherian scheme $T$ are quasi-compact, so this ideal is the kernel itself. On either site put $F_\tau=v_{\tau,!}c_{\tau,*}$ and $E_\tau=i_{\tau,*}u_{\tau,!}$. Let $q_\tau:F_\tau\xrightarrow{\sim}E_\tau$ be the termwise normalized identification restricting to the identity on $S$ [lem-sfb-etale-locally-closed-extension-comparison, lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence]. For every $L\in D^+(S_e,A)$ define
$$\Delta_L=v_{p,!}(\delta_{c,L})o_{v,c_{e,*}L},\qquad B_L=i_{p,*}(o_{u,L})\delta_{i,u_{e,!}L}.$$
These are natural isomorphisms, and their specified maps satisfy
$$q_{p,C_SL}\Delta_L=B_LC_T(q_{e,L}).$$
The closed and open restriction identifications used here agree through the canonical pullback compositor for $s$. In particular, for a second factorization $s=v'\circ c'$, put $t_\tau=(q'_\tau)^{-1}q_\tau:F_\tau\xrightarrow{\sim}F'_\tau$. Then
$$t_{p,C_SL}\Delta_L=\Delta'_LC_T(t_{e,L}).$$
The $t_\tau$ are the identity-normalized change-of-factorization maps and obey identity and cocycle laws.

proof.text: First $V$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. A closed immersion is affine-locally a quotient $R\to R/I$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]; this algebra is generated by the empty set, and its affine spectrum is quasi-compact, so the immersion is finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $i$ over $T$, and to $c$ over $V$: $\bar S$ and $S$ are Noetherian. Thus the normalization lemma applies to all four factors. Use the given closure factorization and the given normalized $q_e,q_p$. The etale closure identification is supplied by [lem-sfb-etale-locally-closed-extension-comparison], inverted to the direction $F_e\to E_e$; [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence] supplies the pro-etale identification and exactness of the pro-etale extension factors. The closed direct images on both sites are exact and their derived comparisons equal the termwise mates by [lem-sf-derived-immersion-comparison-normalization]. Etale open extension is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. Thus the exact-factor cohomology formula [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] shows that $c_{e,*}L$ and $u_{e,!}L$ are bounded below whenever $L$ is. All occurrences of the named closed comparison in the statement therefore have admissible inputs. The given open comparison and the named closed mate are natural isomorphisms, so their whiskered composites $\Delta$ and $B$ are natural isomorphisms. Exact functors preserve inverses, so whiskering introduces no further hypothesis.

proof.text: Write $r_{F,\tau}:s_\tau^*F_\tau\cong1$ for restriction identified as $c_\tau^*v_\tau^*v_{\tau,!}c_{\tau,*}$, followed by the inverse open unit and the closed counit. Likewise let $r_{E,\tau}:s_\tau^*E_\tau\cong1$ use $u_\tau^*i_\tau^*i_{\tau,*}u_{\tau,!}$, the closed counit and the inverse open unit. These are invertible by [lem-sf-derived-immersion-comparison-normalization]. The normalization of the given $q_\tau$ is exactly $r_{E,\tau,L}s_\tau^*(q_{\tau,L})=r_{F,\tau,L}$. The pullback compositor in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies $a_s:C_Ss_e^*\cong s_p^*C_T$ with the successive $a_v,a_c$, and also with the successive $a_i,a_u$, after the respective site pullback compositors. Thus all following formulas use the same $a_s$, rather than two arbitrarily chosen restriction identifications.

proof.text:
The open unit equation of [lem-sf-derived-immersion-comparison-normalization], after multiplying by the inverse units, says that restriction of $o_v$ is the identity under those units. Apply $c_p^*$ and then the closed counit to the restriction of $\Delta_L=v_{p,!}(\delta_{c,L})o_{v,c_{e,*}L}$. The open equation removes $o_v$ and the $v^*v_!$ factors. What remains is precisely the closed normalization equation $\varepsilon^p_c c_p^*(\delta_{c,L})a_{c,c_{e,*}L}=C_S(\varepsilon^e_c)$. Consequently
$$r_{F,p,C_SL}\,s_p^*(\Delta_L)\,a_{s,F_eL}=C_S(r_{F,e,L}).$$
The pullback composition clause in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] is what identifies the two successive pullback comparisons with the displayed $a_s$. Each substitution is an equality of the specified maps, not just an identification of their objects.

source.place: Second proof paragraph: locally closed comparison; normalized open/closed extension maps and their closure-factorization compatibility.

proof.text:
For $B_L=i_{p,*}(o_{u,L})\delta_{i,u_{e,!}L}$, first apply $i_p^*$ and its closed counit. Naturality of that counit moves $i_p^*i_{p,*}(o_u)$ across it; the closed normalization equation removes $\delta_i$ and replaces the remaining closed counit by its $C_{\bar S}$ image. Next apply $u_p^*$ and the inverse open unit. The open unit equation removes $o_u$. With the pullback compositor from [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], this gives
$$r_{E,p,C_SL}\,s_p^*(B_L)\,a_{s,E_eL}=C_S(r_{E,e,L}).$$
These are the same closed counits and open units as in step 2, by [lem-sf-derived-immersion-comparison-normalization]. This also proves the claimed agreement of the closed and open restriction identifications through the compositor for $s$.

proof.text:
Set $f=q_{p,C_SL}\Delta_L$ and $g=B_LC_T(q_{e,L})$, both maps $C_TF_eL\to E_pC_SL$. Step 2 and step 3 give
$$r_{E,p,C_SL}s_p^*(f)a_{s,F_eL}=C_S(r_{F,e,L}).$$
Naturality of $a_s$ at $q_{e,L}$, step 4, and the etale normalization in step 2 give
$$r_{E,p,C_SL}s_p^*(g)a_{s,F_eL}=C_S(r_{E,e,L})C_S(s_e^*q_{e,L})=C_S(r_{F,e,L}).$$
Cancel the invertible outer maps, giving $s_p^*f=s_p^*g$. To use faithfulness on precisely its stated domain, precompose both maps by $\Delta_L^{-1}$ and postcompose by $q_{p,C_SL}^{-1}$. They become endomorphisms of $F_pC_SL$. Restriction on this Hom set is injective by the Hom bijection of [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence]. The endomorphisms agree, so cancellation gives $f=g$, the desired closure square. Here the coefficient sheaf for that theorem is the constant $A_T$, whose inverse image is the constant $A_S$; the base $T$ is Noetherian as required.

proof.text:
Apply the established equation also to the second factorization, using the same closure and hence the same $B$. Then
$$t_{p,C_SL}\Delta_L=(q'_{p,C_SL})^{-1}q_{p,C_SL}\Delta_L=(q'_{p,C_SL})^{-1}B_LC_T(q_{e,L})=\Delta'_LC_T((q'_{e,L})^{-1})C_T(q_{e,L})=\Delta'_LC_T(t_{e,L}).$$
Both $q_\tau$ and $q'_\tau$ restrict to the identity, so their quotient $t_\tau$ does also. They are precisely the normalized change maps through the common closure. For three factorizations, writing $t^{ab}_\tau=(q^b_\tau)^{-1}q^a_\tau$ gives $t^{bc}_\tau t^{ab}_\tau=(q^c_\tau)^{-1}q^b_\tau(q^b_\tau)^{-1}q^a_\tau=t^{ac}_\tau$; $t^{aa}_\tau=1$ follows by inverse cancellation. All these formulas hold termwise and on derived categories. If $S$ is empty, if $s$ is open or closed, or if $A$ is the zero ring, the same units, counits and inverse cancellations apply; no nonempty support or nonzero coefficient assumption was used.
